clue.text: He's far gone

parts.note: a man's first name doubles as a plural noun of distance, so the bloke is one who is a long way off

explanation.surface: Someone has wandered off, or lost his wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far gone' suggests madness or drunkenness; here it is plain distance, and 'He' points to a man's first name that is also a measure of length in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A man named for a unit of distance is, read as a plural, a long way away: an idiom for being remote.

clue.text: Wrong park for a Women's Lib demo

definitions.text: Wrong park for a Women's Lib demo

parts.words: Wrong park for a Women's Lib demo
parts.note: the Jane Austen novel title begins with a word that reads as a male's ground, a poor venue for feminists

explanation.surface: Feminist marchers have picked an unsuitable park.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's novel is Mansfield Park; read as MAN'S FIELD it is the last place a women's movement would rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's Mansfield Park, split into a man's field, suits male rather than female campaigners.

clue.text: Down town with George Eliot

explanation.surface: A Sussex town, and the man who lived with the novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, under the South Downs. G. H. Lewes lived with the novelist George Eliot for over twenty years.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is a town in the South Downs, and George Henry Lewes was George Eliot's partner.

clue.text: Cast off all that's bad Not these females

definitions.text: Cast off all that's bad Not these females

parts.words: Cast off all that's bad Not these females
parts.note: the hyphenated term for wicked women splits into a verb for discarding and a noun for wrongs, which such women would never do

explanation.surface: An urging to reform, with an aside that these women won't.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as SHED EVILS, to cast off all that's bad, which wicked women are the last to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful, wicked women are called devils, here in their female form.

clue.text: The Ripper's blade truck drivers fear

explanation.surface: Jack the Ripper's weapon and a lorry driver's nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper's weapon would be Jack's knife; an articulated lorry folding on itself in a skid is what drivers dread.

clue.text: Ten jigs can get 11 going

definitions.note: 11 across is the clue for Shakespeare's clown, and him going means being at work joking

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be made into another word, so they are to be reordered

explanation.surface: Ten dances could rouse the clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can get' signals rearranging TEN JIGS. The definition refers to 11 across, Feste the clown: him in action is jesting.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown at work is joking, so a fool in action is engaged in banter.

clue.text: Money for the Japanese in sugar production ? No, spice

indicators.note: the money goes inside the word for sugar production

parts.note: sugar is produced from cane
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A question whether Japanese money is behind sugar output, answered by a mention of spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The question mark and 'No' play on the surface: the clue asks about Japanese money in sugar, then says the answer is a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper used as a seasoning.

clue.text: A ball released from a spell

definitions.text: A ball released from a spell

parts.words: A ball released from a spell
parts.note: in the old northern game of knur and spell a wooden ball is flung up from a sprung trap called the spell

explanation.surface: Something round is freed from an enchantment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' is not magic: in the Yorkshire game knur and spell, a ball (knur or knurr) is released from a sprung device, the spell, and struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A knurr is the small wooden ball in the old game of knur and spell.

clue.text: Concentrated in ' at least twenty, I have

parts.note: two or more tens make at least twenty
I have is contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have something concentrated in at least twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at least twenty' is TENS, more than one ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is highly focused effort crammed into a short time.

clue.text: Not what you'd ca' canny

parts.note: written in Scots style; what you would not call canny is uncanny, and the Scots-born word for uncanny fits

explanation.surface: A Scot's remark that something is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ca' canny' is Scots for go carefully; here 'ca'' is just 'call'. What you wouldn't call canny is uncanny, and the word for that is of Scottish origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird and unnatural is uncanny, the opposite of canny.

clue.text: Latest in U.S. knitwear

definitions.note: the definition stands for a part of the US rather than the country itself

parts.note: the latest thing is the new thing
a jersey is a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: The newest fashion in American woollens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the answer is a place in the U.S., one of its states.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty states of the American union.

clue.text: Make an extremist speech ?

parts.note: the verb meaning to say aloud is spelt like the adjective meaning total or extreme, so an 'extremist' could be one who speaks

explanation.surface: A radical takes the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective meaning complete or extreme ('an utter fool') is spelt like the verb for speaking, so speaking is what an 'extreme' person does.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or voice words is the plain sense; the adjective twin means absolute, hence the 'extremist'.

clue.text: The clown is not exempt from life's temptations

indicators.note: the clown is caught up in the following words, so his letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: Even the jester is subject to the ordinary lures of living.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'liFE'S TEmptations'. Feste is the clown in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Feste is the fool in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a professional comic.

clue.text: That pre-fall bliss

parts.note: the proverb says that not knowing is bliss, and before the Fall in Eden Adam and Eve had not eaten from the tree of knowledge

explanation.surface: The happy state of Eden before the Fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Two strands: the proverb 'where ___ is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise', and Eden, where innocence lasted until the fruit of the tree of knowledge was eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of knowledge is the proverb's bliss, and Adam and Eve lacked it until they ate the forbidden fruit.

clue.text: On' your hearing this, madam it just depends

definitions.text: On' your hearing this, madam it just depends

parts.words: On' your hearing this, madam it just depends
parts.note: a piece of jewellery worn on the organ of hearing literally depends, that is hangs down, from it

explanation.surface: A man tells a lady that the outcome turns on what she hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depends' is used in its old sense of hangs down, and 'hearing' means the ear, not the act of listening.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel worn on the lobe hangs from the ear, so it depends in the old sense of dangling.

clue.text: Crusty Mr McGregor's favourite dish maybe

definitions.text: Crusty Mr McGregor's favourite dish maybe

parts.words: Crusty Mr McGregor's favourite dish maybe
parts.note: the gardener in Beatrix Potter's tales was a bad-tempered man whose wife baked Peter's father into pastry

explanation.surface: A grumpy gardener's best-loved meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Beatrix Potter's The Tale of Peter Rabbit, Peter's father was put in a pie by Mrs McGregor. 'Crusty' means both grumpy and with pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry dish of the animal Mr McGregor chased round his garden would suit him.

clue.text: For this man his glen may be over the border

definitions.text: For this man his glen may be over the border

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could become a different word, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from south of Scotland would find a glen in foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals rearranging HIS GLEN. For a man of England a glen, a Scottish valley, lies over the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of England would have to cross into Scotland to find a glen: a description of nationality.

clue.text: Is one contradictory who speaks of profit ?

parts.note: gain means profit
one who says something is a sayer

explanation.surface: A question whether a person who talks of profit is the contrary type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link: a sayer of gain. To gainsay is to deny or contradict.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny, so a gainsayer is someone who argues against.

clue.text: Sudden heat that can cause a breeze

definitions.text: Sudden heat that can cause a breeze

parts.words: Sudden heat that can cause a breeze
parts.note: a rash temper flaring up is quickness of anger, and rushing about stirs the air

explanation.surface: A burst of warmth that stirs up wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' is temper and 'sudden' is rash: rashness. 'Breeze' also means a quarrel, which a quick temper can start.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashness or quickness of temper is the noun from hasty.

clue.text: Composer inclined to be parting from the conductor ?

definitions.text: Composer inclined to be parting from the conductor ?

parts.words: Composer inclined to be parting from the conductor
parts.note: the French composer's name splits into a prefix of leaving, the vehicle, and a suffix meaning inclined to, so someone getting off where a ticket collector works

explanation.surface: A composer is ready to walk out on the man with the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: The conductor is not the orchestra's but the one collecting fares on a bus: the name reads as DE (off) + BUS + SY (inclined to).
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was a French composer, and his name reads as getting off a bus.

clue.text: The sound is above the bay

definitions.text: The sound is above the bay

parts.words: The sound is above the bay
parts.note: the sharp bark of a small dog is higher pitched than the deep howl of a hound

explanation.surface: Coastal geography: a strait lies north of a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' and 'bay' look like coastal geography but are dog noises: a little dog's shrill barking is pitched above a hound's deep bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrill barking by a small dog is higher pitched than a hound's howl.

clue.text: Castle walls — not bridges

parts.note: the outer walls of a fortress share a name with a prefabricated military crossing, which the clue rules out

explanation.surface: A note that a castle's defences, not its bridges, are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bailey bridge is a portable steel bridge from the Second World War; the clue rules it out and wants the walls or courts of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailey is the outer wall or courtyard of a medieval fortification.

clue.text: Gas going up all round

parts.note: a gasbag that rises and is spherical; the phrase all round also sits in its spelling

explanation.surface: Gas is rising everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A balloon is filled with gas, rises, and is round.
explanation.definitionFit: A round envelope filled with light gas floats upwards.

clue.text: The head commands interest

explanation.surface: The headmaster demands attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal is the chief of a college; it is also the capital sum that earns interest from a bank.

clue.text: Piano only convertible to grid-iron ?

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: the letters can be converted into another word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a soft instrument could become a gridiron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' signals rearranging P + ONLY. 'Grid-iron' means a steel tower of the National Grid carrying power lines, not American football.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel lattice tower carrying the electricity grid's cables is an iron structure of the grid.

clue.text: Cut-water

parts.note: a man-made waterway is a channel cut through land; in Britain such a waterway is called a cut

explanation.walkthrough: A cutwater is a ship's prow, but split it as cut water: a waterway dug through land, which in Britain is called a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial waterway is a channel dug through the land.

clue.text: "Where my caravan has rested "

parts.note: the title of an Edwardian ballad, read as a description of an inn for travelling merchants' camel trains

explanation.surface: A line from the old popular song about a caravan's resting place.
explanation.walkthrough: The caravan is a camel train in the East, not a holiday trailer; its resting place is the inn of a caravanserai.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is an Eastern inn where camel trains stop overnight.

clue.text: Brings up, is uppish

explanation.surface: Raising children, or putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to raise a child; a horse that rears lifts itself up on its hind legs.

clue.text: Miss R. R. Hood's least favoured flower ?

definitions.text: Miss R. R. Hood's least favoured flower ?

parts.words: Miss R. R. Hood's least favoured flower
parts.note: Little Red Riding Hood was menaced by a wolf, and this garden plant's name echoes the adjective meaning wolfish

explanation.surface: Red Riding Hood's least favourite bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower's name comes from Latin lupus, wolf, and Red Riding Hood's enemy was the wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a tall garden flower whose name comes from the Latin for wolf.

clue.text: This is no way to have your dreams come true

definitions.text: This is no way to have your dreams come true

parts.words: This is no way to have your dreams come true
parts.note: in Homer and Virgil false dreams pass through one portal of carved tusk, true ones through one of horn

explanation.surface: Advice that this route will not fulfil your hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey and the Aeneid, deceptive dreams come through a gate of ivory and true ones through a gate of horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical myth says dreams through this portal are deceptive, never fulfilled.

clue.text: Sharpshooter from the sewer ?

parts.note: a sewer is one who sews, whose tool is sharp; the firearm takes its name from its firing pin

explanation.surface: A sniper emerges from the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is someone who sews, not a drain. The needle gun was a 19th-century Prussian rifle fired by a needle-like pin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dreyse needle gun was a rifle firing by a long pin; a seamstress's tool shares its name.

clue.text: Flowers that induce showers

parts.note: the perforated spout of a watering can bears the name of a garden bloom, and it makes water fall in drops

explanation.surface: Blooms that bring on the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The perforated nozzle on a watering can is called a rose, so roses produce showers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is both a garden bloom and the sprinkler head on a watering can.
